# Research Software Sustainability

Exploration cluster on how research code survives its authors: maintenance, funding, credit, and the practices that keep a tool usable after the PhD student or postdoc who wrote it leaves.

## Why We Are Reading This

The trigger was concrete. When [[felix-achterberg]] left for industry in 2025-08, the single-cell CNV code from the [[single-cell-cnv-pilot]] had one author, no tests and a hard-coded path to his home directory on Kestrel. The pilot was finished, so nothing broke, but [[tobias-wren]] spent four days in 2025-09 making it rerunnable for the archive. Since then the [[nextflow-pipeline-migration]] and the move to [[halyard-cluster]] have forced the same question for every tool we use. The cluster informs group practice; it is unlikely to become a research Project.

## What We Have Learned So Far

- Robustness and clean code are cheap habits with large returns: [[taschuk-2017-ten-simple-rules-robust-research-software]], [[hunter-zinck-2021-ten-simple-rules-clean-reliable-software]]. Most of their rules are now in our nf-test conventions.
- Small labs can adopt real development process without a software team: [[crusoe-2016-sustainable-software-small-biology-lab]] is the closest analogue to us.
- FAIR principles for software and their user-centred extension: [[barker-2022-fair-principles-research-software]], [[sonabend-2024-fair-use4os]].
- The structural problem is careers and funding, not technique: [[westner-2025-perilous-state-open-source-neuroscience-software]], [[jensen-2025-research-software-funding-survey]], [[goth-2024-research-software-engineer-competencies]].
- Our own numbers: [[group-software-inventory]] and the institute survey led by [[nikolai-petrov]] ([[corvane-rse-survey-2025]]).

## Concepts and Stances

- [[software-bus-factor]]: we count it per tool in the inventory.
- [[every-group-tool-needs-two-maintainers]]: Ines's working rule since 2025-11.
- Open: [[who-maintains-group-software-after-people-leave]].

## Promotion Status

Unlikely to become a Project. Its outputs go into the [[lab-data-management-plan]] revision and onboarding material for [[owen-mcallister]]. A possible exception: a shared RSE post with Nikolai's team, if the Aurora grant budget allows it, would be tracked under [[aurora-programme-grant-2027]].

## Open Thread

The cluster's one live disagreement is about archived code: [[tobias-wren]] wants every archived tool kept rerunnable for five years in a frozen Apptainer image, while Ines thinks a documented container plus the exact inputs is enough for code nobody plans to extend.
